subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Simplification and Mapping
description: A quick, practical guide to Simplification and Mapping.

hook.text: Choosing a phone plan with 47 options and 12 variables paralyzes people. Simplify to 3 plans and they decide in minutes.

buildup.text: Good choice architecture maps complex attributes to understandable outcomes. Don't show megapixels. Show photo quality.

discovery.text: Simplification matters because cognitive overload leads to either bad decisions or no decisions at all.

twist.text: Sweden's school voucher system offered hundreds of options. Instead of choosing wisely, parents picked the nearest.

climax.text: To help people choose well, reduce the number of options and translate technical specs into real outcomes.

quiz.question: What is mapping in choice architecture?
options: Translating complex attributes into understandable outcomes
Giving people more options to choose from

details.summary: Simplification reduces the cognitive load of making good decisions by translating complex information into clear, actionable formats. Mapping translates technical attributes into outcomes people actually care about, like converting megapixels into print quality or data plans into hours of streaming.
details.whyItMatters: Many poor decisions result from inability to process complex information rather than poor preferences. When nutrition labels, financial products, and energy ratings are simplified and mapped to meaningful outcomes, people make choices that better.
takeaways: Complex information can be translated into formats people actually understand
Mapping converts technical attributes into outcomes people care about
Simplification reduces errors caused by cognitive overload rather than poor preferences

faq.question: What is the difference between simplification and mapping in nudge design?
faq.answer: Simplification reduces the amount and complexity of information presented. Mapping translates technical information into outcomes that matter to the user. A simplified phone plan shows fewer options; a mapped phone plan shows hours of streaming rather than gigabytes of data.

faq.question: Can simplification go too far?
faq.answer: Yes. Oversimplification can hide important differences between options or prevent informed comparison. The goal is to remove unnecessary complexity while preserving the information needed to distinguish meaningfully between options. Star ratings can oversimplify complex quality.
